---
title: "Quiz: speed, MSD and modes of motion"
---

Short questions to test your understanding. Try each on paper first, then open the answer.

---

**Q1.** A track goes (0, 0) → (3, 0) → (3, 4). What are its path length, net displacement and straightness?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Straightness = net displacement / path length.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Path length 3 + 4 = 7; net displacement $\sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$; straightness 5/7 = 0.71.
:::

---

**Q2.** You measure the "speed" of a diffusing particle at 10 frames per second and at 100 frames per second. Which value is larger, and by how much?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
For random motion the displacement grows as √Δt.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
At 100 frames per second: Δt is 10 times shorter, the step only $\sqrt{10}$ times shorter, so the apparent speed is $\sqrt{10} \approx 3.2$ times larger. Random motion has no well-defined speed; report D.
:::

---

**Q3.** Sketch the MSD against lag for free diffusion, directed motion and confined motion. What do the three look like on log–log axes?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Line, upward curve, plateau.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Free diffusion: a straight line through the origin (slope 1 on log–log axes). Directed: curves upward, slope approaching 2 on log–log axes at long lags. Confined: rises, then levels off at a plateau (slope falling to 0 on log–log axes).
:::

---

**Q4.** The MSD of a free particle in 2D has slope 0.4 µm²/s. What is D?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
In $d$ dimensions the slope is $2dD$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
In 2D the slope is $4D$, so $D = 0.4/4 = 0.1$ µm²/s.
:::

---

**Q5.** Your fitted MSD line has a positive intercept instead of passing through 0. What is the most likely cause, and how large is the effect for σ = 20 nm?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Every position has its own error.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Localisation error: it adds $4\sigma^2$ in 2D to every lag. For σ = 20 nm = 0.02 µm: $4 \cdot 0.0004 = 0.0016$ µm². (Motion blur during the exposure lowers the intercept; the two can partly cancel.)
:::

---

**Q6.** Why should you fit only the first part of the MSD curve?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
How many pairs does the longest lag have?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
At long lags there are only a few (overlapping) pairs, so the MSD values there are very noisy; at the longest lag of a track there is a single pair. The first lags are averages of many pairs and carry most of the information about D.
:::

---

**Q7.** At high particle density, linking errors become frequent. Does the measured D go up or down? Why?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Which links does a tracker prefer when it is unsure?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Down. The tracker prefers short links: when a particle makes a long jump, a closer wrong particle is chosen, so long steps are replaced by shorter ones and the MSD (and D) is under-estimated.
:::

---

**Q8.** *(math)* Show that for a 2D random walk with steps of variance $2D\Delta t$ per axis, $\text{MSD}(n\Delta t) = 4Dn\Delta t$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Variances of independent steps add.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The displacement over $n$ frames is the sum of $n$ independent steps with mean 0. Per axis its variance is $n \cdot 2D\Delta t$; the MSD is the sum over the two axes: $2 \cdot 2Dn\Delta t = 4D\tau$ with $\tau = n\Delta t$.
:::
